q: What is a project management methodology?
options: A structured approach to planning, executing, and completing projects
A list of everyone affected by a project
A certification that proves a manager's credibility
The final report written when a project closes
explanation: A methodology is a structured approach with frameworks, principles, and practices for planning, executing, and completing projects. A list of affected people is a stakeholder register, and PMP is a certification.

q: Which organization issues PMBOK?
options: International Organization for Standardization (ISO)
UK government
Project Management Institute (PMI)
A group of software developers in 2001
explanation: PMBOK is issued by PMI. ISO publishes ISO 21500, the UK government developed PRINCE2, and software developers wrote the Agile Manifesto in 2001.

q: What does PRINCE2 stand for?
options: Project Integration in Controlled Environments
PRojects IN Controlled Environments
Process Review In Certified Engineering
PRoject INitiation and Closing Environment
explanation: PRINCE2 stands for PRojects IN Controlled Environments. 'Project Integration' is a common mix-up with the Integration knowledge area.

q: In Agile, what is an iteration or sprint?
options: The full plan written before any work starts
A board column showing work in progress
A formal request to change the project scope
A short cycle of work that produces a functional product or feature to be reviewed
explanation: Agile divides work into iterations or sprints, each producing something functional that is reviewed and adjusted from stakeholder feedback. Agile avoids planning everything up front.

q: What is scope creep?
options: Uncontrolled changes to the project scope
A delay caused by a missing supplier
Gradual improvement of a product through iterations
Running out of budget before closing
explanation: Scope creep is uncontrolled change to the project scope, which Scope Management prevents. Gradual improvement through iterations is Agile's planned approach, not scope creep.

q: Which Agile framework focuses on visualizing the workflow and limiting work in progress?
options: Scrum
Extreme Programming (XP)
Kanban
PRINCE2
explanation: Kanban visualizes workflow and limits work in progress, using continuous flow. Scrum uses sprints, XP focuses on technical coding practices, and PRINCE2 is not an Agile framework.

q: In Scrum, who defines the project requirements and priorities?
options: Scrum Master
Development Team
Project sponsor
Product Owner
explanation: The Product Owner defines requirements and priorities. The Scrum Master facilitates the process and removes obstacles, and the Development Team does the work.

q: Which knowledge area involves acquiring goods and services from external vendors through contract negotiation and supplier selection?
options: Resource Management
Procurement Management
Stakeholder Management
Cost Management
explanation: Procurement Management covers buying from external vendors, including contract negotiation, supplier selection, and vendor management. Resource Management uses the team and materials efficiently.

q: How does PMBOK organize project management?
options: Into five process groups and ten knowledge areas
Into seven principles, seven themes, and seven processes
Into four values and twelve principles
Into sprints of 2 to 4 weeks
explanation: PMBOK uses five process groups and ten knowledge areas. Seven principles, themes, and processes are PRINCE2; four values and twelve principles are the Agile Manifesto; sprints are Scrum.

q: What are the three key components of PRINCE2?
options: Values, principles, and sprints
Seven Principles, Seven Themes, and Seven Processes
Process groups, knowledge areas, and certification
To Do, In Progress, and Done
explanation: PRINCE2's key components are seven principles, seven themes, and seven processes. Process groups and knowledge areas belong to PMBOK, and To Do, In Progress, Done are Kanban columns.

q: How long is a Scrum sprint usually?
options: 1 to 2 days
6 to 12 months
2 to 4 weeks
There is no fixed length; work flows continuously
explanation: Scrum sprints are usually 2 to 4 weeks and produce a potentially shippable increment. Continuous flow with no fixed length describes Kanban.

q: How many values and principles does the Agile Manifesto have?
options: Twelve values and four principles
Seven values and seven principles
Five values and ten principles
Four values and twelve principles
explanation: The Agile Manifesto has four values and twelve principles. Swapping the two numbers is a common mistake, and five and ten are PMBOK's process groups and knowledge areas.

q: Which set lists technical practices emphasized by Extreme Programming (XP)?
options: Test-driven development, pair programming, continuous integration
Business case, risk, quality, change
Scope planning, definition, verification, control
Cost estimating, budgeting, monitoring
explanation: XP emphasizes test-driven development, pair programming, and continuous integration. Business case, risk, quality, change are PRINCE2 themes; the other two sets are Scope and Cost Management activities.

q: What is the order of PMBOK's five process groups?
options: Planning, Initiating, Executing, Closing, Monitoring and Controlling
Initiating, Planning, Executing, Monitoring and Controlling, Closing
Initiating, Executing, Planning, Monitoring and Controlling, Closing
Initiating, Planning, Monitoring and Controlling, Executing, Closing
explanation: Initiating defines and authorizes, Planning sets scope and procedures, Executing does the work, Monitoring and Controlling tracks performance, and Closing formally ends the project.

q: What is the order of activities in Schedule Management?
options: Estimate durations, define tasks, develop the schedule, sequence tasks
Develop the schedule, define tasks, sequence tasks, estimate durations
Define tasks, sequence them, estimate their durations, develop and monitor the schedule
Sequence tasks, estimate durations, define tasks, develop the schedule
explanation: You must define tasks before you can sequence them, estimate how long each takes, and only then build the schedule that is monitored. Estimating durations of tasks not yet defined is impossible.

q: In the Agile burger example, what is the order of one improvement cycle?
options: Get feedback, deliver the final burger, plan the recipe, test
Plan the full recipe once, cook all versions, then ask customers
Ask customers, close the project, cook the burger, add bacon
Make a burger, share it with a customer, get feedback, make the next iteration with changes
explanation: Agile cycles through building, testing with customers, learning from feedback, and iterating. Planning everything once before asking customers is the traditional approach Agile avoids.

q: What is the order of the phases in ISO 21500's project life cycle?
options: Initiating, Planning, Implementing, Controlling, Closing
Planning, Initiating, Controlling, Implementing, Closing
Starting up, Directing, Initiating, Controlling a Stage, Closing
To Do, In Progress, Done
explanation: ISO 21500 covers phases similar to PMBOK: Initiating, Planning, Implementing, Controlling, Closing. Starting up and Directing are PRINCE2 processes, and To Do, In Progress, Done are Kanban columns.

q: Which statement about ISO 21500 is NOT true?
options: It is published by the International Organization for Standardization
It emphasizes aligning projects with organizational strategy
It was developed by the UK government and focuses on business justification
It aligns closely with PMBOK
explanation: The UK government and business justification describe PRINCE2, not ISO 21500. ISO 21500 is from ISO, aligns with PMBOK, and stresses organizational strategy.

q: Which pairing of a Scrum role and its duty is mismatched?
options: Product Owner: defines requirements and priorities
Scrum Master: completes the work and creates the deliverables
Development Team: completes the work and creates the deliverables
Scrum Master: facilitates the process and resolves obstacles
explanation: The Scrum Master facilitates and removes obstacles; completing the work is the Development Team's job. The other three pairs are correct.

q: Which statement about Kanban is NOT true?
options: It uses a board with columns for stages of work
It limits work in progress to improve efficiency
It visualizes the workflow
It organizes work into fixed sprints of 2 to 4 weeks
explanation: Fixed sprints of 2 to 4 weeks belong to Scrum. Kanban allows continuous flow rather than defined sprints.

q: Which pairing of a methodology and its origin or focus is mismatched?
options: Agile Manifesto: written by the UK government for the public sector
PMBOK: issued by PMI, consistent across industries
PRINCE2: developed by the UK government, focuses on business justification
ISO 21500: published by ISO, focuses on organizational strategy
explanation: The Agile Manifesto was introduced in 2001 by a group of software developers. The UK government developed PRINCE2. The other three pairs are correct.

q: A government agency wants a methodology where every project must keep a justified business case, with clear roles and control over each stage. Which fits best?
options: Kanban
PRINCE2
Extreme Programming (XP)
Agile Manifesto
explanation: PRINCE2 focuses on business justification, defined roles, and control over each phase, and is highly valued in government and the public sector. Kanban and XP are Agile frameworks for flexible work.

q: A game studio expects player feedback to keep changing the requirements, and wants to release playable versions often. Which approach fits best?
options: A traditional plan where most planning happens before the project begins
A methodology chosen mainly for business case control
Agile, using short iterations and customer feedback
Procurement Management
explanation: Agile suits projects where requirements are likely to change, such as software and game development, through iterative delivery and feedback. Traditional methods assume predictable factors.

q: During a school building project, the manager notices that rooms keep being added without approval, and the deadline keeps slipping. Which knowledge area failed, and what is the problem called?
options: Procurement Management; vendor failure
Risk Management; mitigation
Communication Management; information overload
Scope Management; scope creep
explanation: Uncontrolled additions to what the project must deliver are scope creep, which Scope Management prevents through scope planning, definition, verification, and control.

q: A student writes: 'PMBOK, issued by ISO, has 5 process groups and 10 knowledge areas, and its certification is the PMP.' What is the error?
options: PMBOK is issued by PMI, not ISO
PMBOK has 7 process groups
PMBOK has 12 knowledge areas
The PMP belongs to PRINCE2
explanation: PMBOK comes from the Project Management Institute (PMI). ISO publishes ISO 21500. The counts (5 and 10) and the PMP certification are correct.

q: A reviewer lists the ten knowledge areas as: Scope, Time, Cost, Quality, Resource, Communication, Risk, Procurement, Stakeholder, and Change. What is wrong?
options: Time should be Schedule, so only nine are valid
Change is not a knowledge area; the missing tenth area is Integration
Stakeholder is not a knowledge area; it should be Sponsor
Nothing is wrong; Change replaces Integration in PMBOK
explanation: Change is a PRINCE2 theme, not a knowledge area. The tenth area is Integration, which coordinates all the others. Time and Schedule are two names for the same area.

q: In a house renovation, the manager (1) buys kitchen cabinets from a supplier, then (2) checks that the delivered appliances are stainless steel as specified, then (3) plans for the chance that a worker gets injured. Which knowledge areas apply, in order?
options: Resource, Scope, Risk
Cost, Quality, Stakeholder
Procurement, Quality, Risk
Procurement, Integration, Communication
explanation: Buying from a supplier is Procurement, checking appliances meet the specification is Quality, and planning for possible injury is Risk Management.

q: A team's board has columns To Do, In Progress, and Done, with no fixed cycles. Separately, the team writes tests before coding and two programmers share one computer. Which two Agile frameworks are being used?
options: Scrum, then PRINCE2
Scrum, then Kanban
Kanban, then Scrum
Kanban, then Extreme Programming (XP)
explanation: A board with continuous flow is Kanban. Writing tests first (test-driven development) and two programmers at one computer (pair programming) are XP practices.

q: A café project's manager notices that the scope assumes 6 months of work but only 3 months are available, so they adjust the scope, schedule, and budget so they fit together. Which knowledge area is this, and why?
options: Integration Management, because it makes all the other areas consistent with each other
Schedule Management, because only the timeline changed
Cost Management, because the budget was adjusted
Stakeholder Management, because the owner is affected
explanation: Integration Management checks that scope matches the time available, costs match scope and quality, and all areas are consistent. Here several areas are adjusted together, not just one.

q: Which of these is one of the four Agile Manifesto values?
options: Continued business justification
Responding to change
Alignment with organizational goals
Standardization and adaptability
explanation: Responding to change is an Agile value. Continued business justification is a PRINCE2 principle, and the other two are ISO 21500 core principles.
